subject.title: Control UI fails to load on Firefox desktop behind reverse proxy — CSP blocks Vite runtime eval(), 'Control UI did not start', WebSocket 1006

question: Should this issue remain separate for Firefox reverse-proxy WebSocket 1006 proof, and should the CSP repair require a no-eval/Zod-jitless path rather than allowing unsafe-eval?
rationale: The source evidence overlaps the open CSP/Zod issue, but the proposed easy fix weakens a Control UI security boundary and the reverse-proxy socket symptom is not yet live-proven on current main.

options.title: Keep Separate And Preserve Strict CSP
options.body: Keep this issue open for live Firefox reverse-proxy diagnostics while the CSP repair stays on the strict no-eval path tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78362.

options.title: Fold Into CSP Thread After Proof
options.body: Consolidate this issue into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78362 only if live proof shows the WebSocket 1006 was startup fallout from the CSP/Zod failure.

options.title: Accept Unsafe-Eval Deliberately
options.body: Allow unsafe-eval only if maintainers explicitly accept the wider Control UI script-execution risk with matching browser proof and security rationale.

recommendation.title: Keep Separate And Preserve Strict CSP
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for live Firefox reverse-proxy diagnostics while the CSP repair stays on the strict no-eval path tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78362.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history across Control UI CSP lockdown, bootstrap sharing, and WebSocket origin hardening.
